title: A small, not-so-smart model went from 10% to 99.6% at reading property deeds for $1.15, and it says 'check this line' instead of bluffing
why_read: A concrete, numbers-heavy case study on fine-tuning a small model cheaply to reliably parse error-prone legal land descriptions, with honest reporting of failure modes.
analysis: The author describes fine-tuning a small language model, Qwen3-8B with a LoRA adapter, to accurately parse property deed descriptions that use compass-bearing distance notation, improving accuracy from 10% to 99.6% for about a dollar in training cost. Critically, the system is designed to detect geometric inconsistencies, such as a land parcel that doesn't close back to its starting point, and flag likely transcription errors for human review instead of confidently guessing. This is a good, specific example of practical, cheap LLM fine-tuning paired with a domain-specific validation check, which is a solid engineering pattern beyond just prompting. The reported cost and accuracy numbers give it real evidentiary weight compared to vague AI success claims.
